hero.headline: Trump and Kemp back opposing candidates in Georgia Senate primary
hero.teaser: President Trump and Georgia Governor Brian Kemp support different Republican candidates in the state's Senate primary election.
hero.body:
President Trump and Governor Brian Kemp are on opposite sides as Georgia voters go to the polls to pick a Republican nominee for Senate. Kemp backs former college football coach Derek Dooley while Trump endorses Representative Mike Collins.

The contest pits Trump against the governor of a key swing state in a test of influence within the Republican Party. The primary results will indicate which Republican leader holds more sway with Georgia voters in a race that could affect the balance of power in the Senate.

cards.headline: Trump says US-Iran deal could be released before Friday
cards.teaser: Vice President JD Vance said the agreement is about a page and a half long and covers general terms, with many details to be finalized later.
cards.body:
The US vice president said the Trump administration may release a deal with Iran before the end of the week. Vance described the agreement as very general, spanning roughly a page and a half.

According to Vance, many specifics will need to be worked out after the initial framework is made public.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans withhold support for Trump Iran peace deal
cards.teaser: Republican senators declined to embrace President Trump's announced peace deal with Iran, telling reporters they need more information about the agreement and w.
cards.body:
Republican senators declined to embrace President Trump's announced peace deal with Iran, telling reporters they need more information about the agreement and whether it stops Iran's nuclear program before offering judgment. The hesitation marks a cautious response from Trump's own party following the United States and Israel launching strikes in February that led to a brief military conflict.

The United States and Iran are scheduled to sign a truce agreement on Friday to end hostilities in what officials have described as a brief war between the two nations. Both President Trump and Iranian leaders are known for unpredictable negotiating approaches, and the specifics of the deal have not been made public. Republican allies on Capitol Hill have maintained since the strikes began that they needed to understand the terms of any potential agreement.

The Senate Republican response reflects broader uncertainty about the consequences of the conflict and its resolution. The military engagement between the United States and Iran followed months of rising tensions in the region. Lawmakers from both parties have sought briefings on the negotiations and the framework that would govern relations between Washington and Tehran going forward.

The peace agreement comes at a sensitive political moment, with voters expressing concern about the economic fallout from the conflict. Gas prices rose during the period of military engagement, and Republicans in particular face questions about how the brief war and its aftermath will affect their standing with the electorate. Senate Republicans have indicated they will wait for the full text of the agreement and formal briefings before deciding whether to support the deal.

The White House has not released details about what concessions either side made during negotiations or what verification mechanisms the agreement includes. Republican senators told reporters they consider those details essential to evaluating whether the deal serves American national security interests and prevents Iran from developing nuclear weapons capability.

cards.headline: Warsh Takes Over Federal Reserve Amid Inflation Concerns
cards.teaser: Kevin Warsh begins his tenure as Federal Reserve chairman facing elevated inflation and decisions about potential rate increases.
cards.body:
Kevin M. Warsh stepped into his first Federal Reserve meeting as chairman confronting significant economic challenges. Elevated inflation and the prospect of interest rate increases marked his debut in the role, setting the stage for what could be a difficult balancing act ahead.

The new Fed chairman inherits an economy grappling with price pressures at a time when monetary policy decisions carry heightened consequences. Warsh will need to navigate between controlling inflation and avoiding excessive economic slowdown as he leads the central bank through this period.

cards.headline: B-52 bomber crashes at Edwards Air Force Base in California, killing eight crew members
cards.body:
Eight crew members are presumed dead after a B-52 Stratofortress bomber crashed shortly after takeoff at Edwards Air Force Base in California's Mojave Desert on Monday morning.

The aircraft went down at 11:20 a.m. during what officials described as a routine test mission. Edwards Air Force Base released a statement confirming the crash and noting that "initial indications are that the crash was not survivable." Emergency response personnel responded to the scene, and officials worked to account for all personnel involved in the incident.

The B-52 Stratofortress is a long-range strategic bomber that has served as a cornerstone of the United States Air Force since the 1950s. The aircraft typically carries crews of five members, though configurations can vary based on mission requirements. The bomber involved in this crash was conducting testing operations at the California base, which functions as a primary location for flight testing military aircraft.

Edwards Air Force Base, situated in the Mojave Desert in southern California's Kern County, has served as a center for aerospace testing and development for decades. The base regularly conducts test missions for various military aircraft as part of ongoing maintenance, upgrade, and certification programs. These test flights are standard procedures used to evaluate aircraft performance and systems.

This crash represents one of the deadliest military aviation incidents in recent years. Military officials have not yet released information regarding the cause of the crash or the identities of the crew members killed. The Air Force is expected to launch a formal investigation to determine the factors that contributed to the disaster.

B-52 bombers remain a critical component of the United States' strategic arsenal despite their age. The Air Force has continued to modernize and maintain the fleet while planning to keep the aircraft in service for several additional decades. The service regularly conducts training and testing operations to ensure the bombers remain mission-ready and operationally effective.

The crash occurred during a period when the military continues to rely heavily on the B-52 platform for strategic deterrence and long-range strike capabilities. The aircraft's longevity in service reflects both its robust design and the Air Force's commitment to extending the platform's operational life through ongoing upgrades and maintenance programs.

Investigators will likely examine multiple factors in determining what led to the crash, including aircraft systems, weather conditions, and crew operations. The investigation results will be important for understanding the incident and potentially informing safety improvements across the B-52 fleet.

cards.headline: San Andreas Fault reaches highest stress level in 1,000 years, study finds
cards.body:
The San Andreas Fault has reached its highest stress level in a thousand years, according to a study from the University of Hawaii. The research marks a significant finding for earthquake preparedness efforts along one of the most seismically active fault lines in the United States.

The San Andreas Fault system extends roughly 800 miles through California, forming the boundary between the Pacific and North American tectonic plates. The fault has produced some of the most powerful earthquakes in California history, including the 1906 San Francisco earthquake that killed thousands and the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake that caused widespread damage across the Bay Area.

Stress accumulation along fault lines occurs as tectonic plates grind past each other, building pressure over time until it releases in the form of an earthquake. Scientists monitor these stress levels to better understand seismic risk and potential earthquake timing. The University of Hawaii study indicates that current stress levels exceed any measured over the past millennium, though the research does not predict when the next major earthquake might occur.

The finding carries significant implications for California, where more than 39 million residents live in proximity to the fault system. Major urban centers including Los Angeles, San Francisco, and San Diego sit near or on top of fault segments. Previous major earthquakes along the San Andreas Fault have caused catastrophic damage, and seismologists have long warned that the region remains overdue for another large seismic event.

Earthquake preparedness remains a priority for California state and local governments, which have invested in building code improvements, early warning systems, and public education campaigns. The elevated stress levels documented in the University of Hawaii study underscore the ongoing seismic threat facing California communities and the importance of continued investment in earthquake resilience infrastructure.

cards.headline: Trump administration blocks Anthropic cybersecurity AI models
cards.teaser: The Trump administration forced AI company Anthropic to pull its latest cybersecurity models from the market in a decision that signals government willingness to regulate the AI industry.
cards.body:
Anthropic will disable its most advanced AI models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, following a US government export control directive. The administration ordered the company to suspend access to these models for foreign nationals, citing national security concerns but providing no specific details about the threat.

The government's action focused on concerns that safeguards could be bypassed to identify software vulnerabilities, rather than citing an AI jailbreak or security flaw. The decision signals that AI companies remain subject to government intervention on national security grounds.

hero.headline: Ukraine and Moldova begin formal EU membership talks
hero.body:
Ukraine and Moldova have launched formal accession negotiations with the European Union, marking what officials describe as a historic moment for both countries. Senior EU officials and ministers from both nations met in Luxembourg on Monday to begin substantive talks on the first cluster of EU requirements, covering rule of law and democracy.

The start of negotiations comes after a delay caused by Hungary's previous opposition. Viktor Orban, Hungary's prime minister, had blocked progress on the membership process despite a symbolic decision to open talks in June 2024. The talks moved forward after Hungary's government changed in April, allowing EU member states to reach unanimous agreement last Friday to proceed with negotiations.

Ukraine and Moldova both applied for EU membership shortly after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and the EU granted them candidate status that same year. The formal start of substantive talks means both nations will now begin the lengthy process of adopting thousands of European laws and aligning their institutions with EU standards.

The accession process typically requires candidates to meet strict criteria across numerous policy areas. Opening the first cluster on rule of law and democracy creates a pathway for talks on other areas, including the single market, environmental policy, and economic and social matters. Each member state must ultimately approve any new EU additions.

EU leaders Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa said in a joint statement that they praised "the determination, courage and hard work shown by both countries in advancing reforms, even in the face of immense challenges."

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy responded positively, saying: "Ukraine is doing what is necessary, and it is important that the EU is also keeping its word. The opening of the first cluster is significant political and moral support for our state and our people."

However, EU officials have expressed concern about the pace of reforms. Ukraine has completed only about 15 percent of reforms contained in a ten-point plan agreed in December with EU enlargement commissioner Marta Kos. The plan includes strengthening anti-corruption agencies and reforming judicial appointment processes.

EU officials believe that with sufficient effort, Ukraine could complete technical talks in approximately four years, though they acknowledge that membership ultimately remains a political decision.

Heather Grabbe, a former European Commission adviser on enlargement, said the opening of cluster one was significant but would also serve as a reality check. She noted that Ukraine cannot bypass the lengthy process of adopting and implementing EU laws on its territory.

Ukraine continues to face significant challenges, fighting Russia's ongoing invasion while simultaneously working to meet EU requirements. The country's authorities have made high-profile anti-corruption arrests that EU officials view as positive signs of commitment to reform, though progress on several key areas remains incomplete.

cards.headline: Trump says US-Iran deal could be released before Friday
cards.teaser: Vice President JD Vance said the agreement is about a page and a half long and covers general terms, with many details to be finalized later.
cards.body:
The US vice president said the Trump administration may release a deal with Iran before the end of the week. Vance described the agreement as very general, spanning roughly a page and a half.

According to Vance, many specifics will need to be worked out after the initial framework is made public.

cards.headline: Israel called off major strike on Iran last week, air force chief confirms
cards.teaser: The Israeli Air Force chief confirmed that a planned large-scale attack on Iran was canceled, as Trump warned Israel that Lebanon strikes risk derailing an Iran deal.
cards.body:
Israel's Air Force chief has confirmed that a planned military strike against Iran was cancelled last week. The decision reflected pressure from the Trump administration, which expressed concern that Israeli military operations could derail ongoing diplomatic negotiations with Tehran.

Trump reportedly told Israeli officials that recent strikes in Lebanon were problematic and risked undermining emerging peace talks with Iran. The message signaled the administration's preference for pursuing diplomatic channels over military action at this critical moment in negotiations.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike Moscow oil refinery
cards.teaser: Ukraine hit Moscow's largest refinery with drones despite the facility beginning shutdown procedures before the attack arrived.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck Moscow's biggest oil refinery in an attack that proceeded even as the facility had begun shutting down operations. The Moscow mayor said dozens of Ukrainian drones were downed during the assault on the Russian capital.

Ukraine has continued targeting Russian energy infrastructure as part of its military strategy. A separate attack hit a sea terminal, and Ukrainian officials said they plan to maintain pressure on Russia's industrial and energy facilities.

cards.headline: Japan raises interest rate to highest level in 31 years
cards.teaser: The Bank of Japan increased rates as part of its ongoing shift away from the near-zero policy it maintained for decades.
cards.body:
The Bank of Japan raised its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 1%, marking the highest level in 31 years. The decision reflects efforts to combat inflationary pressures stemming from the Iran war, as companies pass rising oil costs through supply chains at a faster pace.

This latest increase continues Japan's shift away from decades of ultra-loose monetary policy. The central bank has been gradually raising rates from near-zero levels since 2024, signaling a broader normalization of its approach to monetary policy.

cards.headline: India temporarily bans Telegram over exam paper leak
cards.teaser: The government suspended the messaging app after concerns that it facilitated leaks of the NEET medical entrance exam.
cards.body:
India imposed a temporary ban on Telegram following allegations that the platform was used to distribute leaked exam papers. The NEET medical entrance exam had been scrapped earlier after widespread reports of a paper leak, sparking large protests across the country.

The suspension targets concerns about how the messaging service may have enabled the distribution of confidential test materials. The NEET controversy has become a major issue in India, affecting hundreds of thousands of students seeking admission to medical schools.

cards.headline: Nigerian army rescues widow of former general who died in captivity
cards.teaser: Amina Abubakar was freed by military forces after she and her husband were abducted in northwest Nigeria last month.
cards.body:
The Nigerian army has rescued Amina Abubakar, widow of Major General Rabe Abubakar. The couple was abducted in northwest Nigeria late last month.

Maj Gen Abubakar died while in captivity before his wife could be freed. The kidnappings are part of a broader security crisis affecting Nigeria, with armed groups conducting abductions across multiple regions in the northwest and northeast.

cards.headline: Voting officials express concern about Department of Homeland Security role in elections
cards.teaser: Election administrators worry that DHS may seek to undermine results President Trump opposes rather than help secure voting systems.
cards.body:
Voting officials have expressed worry that the Department of Homeland Security may undermine election results rather than serve as a security partner. Their concerns center on whether DHS will work against results that President Trump views unfavorably.

Traditionally, DHS has collaborated with state and local election administrators to protect voting infrastructure from cyber threats and security risks. The shift in officials' perspective reflects growing uncertainty about the federal government's role in election oversight ahead of this year's elections.

cards.headline: Apartment surplus drives move-in deals for renters in some markets
cards.teaser: A construction boom has created an oversupply of apartments, with about 40% of Zillow listings offering incentives like free rent.
cards.body:
About 40% of rental properties listed on Zillow now offer move-in deals, including incentives such as a month of free rent. The trend stems from a construction boom that produced a surplus of apartments in certain parts of the United States.

The availability of deals varies significantly by location. Renters in areas with high levels of new apartment construction are seeing the most competitive offers from landlords seeking to fill units. The shift marks a change from recent years when renters faced limited inventory and rising prices in many markets.

cards.headline: Primaries held in Georgia, Alabama, Oklahoma and Washington DC
cards.teaser: Voters in four states and the District of Columbia cast ballots in primary elections.
cards.body:
Primary elections took place in Georgia, Alabama, Oklahoma and Washington DC. The contests are drawing attention for races where President Trump has backed specific candidates and for battleground state competitions.

The primaries will help determine which candidates advance to general election ballots later this year. Several races are being watched as tests of Trump's influence within the Republican Party. The results will shape the political landscape heading into the general election season.

cards.headline: Brain research center shifts focus to transparent fish for neuroscience studies
cards.teaser: A leading research facility is moving away from fruit flies to study tiny transparent fish to better understand how brains control behavior.
cards.body:
One of the world's leading brain research centers is moving away from fruit flies as its primary research model and turning to a tiny, transparent fish instead. Researchers believe this shift will help them better understand how brains control behavior in animals and humans.

The fish's transparency is a key advantage for neuroscientists. It allows them to directly observe brain activity and neural processes in living organisms, making it easier to study the relationship between brain function and animal behavior.

cards.headline: Vice President Vance says US-Iran deal may be released before Friday
cards.teaser: The agreement is about a page and a half long and covers general terms, with many details to be worked out later.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance said President Trump may release a US-Iran agreement before Friday. The deal is about a page and a half in length and described as very general in nature. The memorandum of understanding, set for a ceremonial signing Friday in Geneva, centers on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting the US naval blockade in the region.

Many specific details still need to be worked out after the initial agreement is made public. The deal includes financial incentives for Iran if it meets certain benchmarks. Senate Republicans have expressed skepticism about the agreement and pressed the White House for more information, citing unanswered questions about the terms and funding involved.

cards.headline: Artist creates belt-themed work addressing discipline in Black households
cards.teaser: Lex Marie has gained attention on social media for artwork that examines physical discipline practices.
cards.body:
Multidisciplinary artist Lex Marie has gained viral attention on TikTok and Instagram for artwork that uses belts to explore discipline within Black households. Based in the DMV area, Marie's pieces directly confront the topic of physical discipline and its role in Black family culture.

The work has sparked online conversations about parenting practices and generational patterns within communities. Through multiple artistic mediums, Marie examines themes of family and community, using the belt as a central visual element to engage audiences with this personal and cultural subject matter.

hero.headline: Japan Raises Interest Rates to Highest Level in 31 Years
hero.body:
The Bank of Japan has lifted its short-term policy rate to 1 percent, up from 0.75 percent, marking the highest borrowing costs the country has seen since 1995. The decision comes as policymakers attempt to control inflation driven by the Iran conflict and its impact on global energy markets.

The quarter-point rate increase reflects the central bank's concern that companies are passing rising oil costs along the supply chain at a relatively fast pace. Despite recent peace negotiations between Washington and Tehran, and despite Japan's core inflation falling to a four-year low of 1.4 percent in April, the Bank of Japan proceeded with the hike. Central bank governor Shinichi Uchida acknowledged that a U.S.-Iran peace memorandum was welcome, but emphasized uncertainty about how quickly oil supplies would recover.

"With underlying inflation approaching 2 percent, it's important to ensure we achieve our target stably," Uchida said at a Tokyo press conference. He noted that while the risk of sharp economic deterioration from the Middle East conflict had diminished, "price rises are broadening, and there is a risk that underlying inflation may deviate from our target."

The rate rise represents a significant shift in Japanese monetary policy. For decades, the Bank of Japan maintained near-zero or negative interest rates to stimulate its economy and combat deflation following the asset bubble that burst in the late 1980s. The central bank began raising rates in 2024, but this latest increase marks a substantial step away from the ultra-loose policies that had long defined Japan's approach.

The move attracted some market relief, as analysts had speculated the increase could have been larger. A 50-basis-point hike had been considered possible. Investment strategist Susannah Streeter noted that while the increase was widely anticipated, it still represents "a step-change in monetary policy for Japan."

The rate increase comes as the Bank of Japan joins other major central banks responding to war-related inflation. The European Central Bank raised its rates last week, while the U.S. Federal Reserve and Bank of England are expected to maintain their current rates at upcoming meetings.

The Japanese stock market reacted positively to the news. The Nikkei share index reached 70,000 points for the first time during Tuesday's trading session, having surged roughly one-third so far this year.

Higher Japanese interest rates carry global implications. Japan's traditionally low rates had made the yen attractive for carry trades, where investors borrow cheaply in one currency to invest in higher-yielding assets elsewhere. Rate increases could prompt shifts in these investment patterns and affect borrowing costs worldwide.

cards.headline: Warsh Takes Over Federal Reserve Amid Inflation Concerns
cards.teaser: Kevin Warsh begins his tenure as Federal Reserve chairman facing elevated inflation and decisions about potential rate increases.
cards.body:
Kevin M. Warsh stepped into his first Federal Reserve meeting as chairman confronting significant economic challenges. Elevated inflation and the prospect of interest rate increases marked his debut in the role, setting the stage for what could be a difficult balancing act ahead.

The new Fed chairman inherits an economy grappling with price pressures at a time when monetary policy decisions carry heightened consequences. Warsh will need to navigate between controlling inflation and avoiding excessive economic slowdown as he leads the central bank through this period.

cards.headline: China Retail Sales Fall for First Time Since Pandemic
cards.teaser: Consumer spending in China declined unexpectedly, highlighting the country's growing dependence on exports as domestic demand weakens.
cards.body:
Retail sales in China posted an unexpected decline, marking the first drop since the Covid pandemic ended. The decrease underscored deepening concerns about domestic consumer demand as Chinese households continue to reduce their spending.

The spending slowdown revealed China's increasing reliance on exports to maintain economic growth. As domestic consumption falters, the country faces challenges in rebalancing its economy away from its traditional export-driven model toward greater internal demand.

cards.headline: Major Banks Cut Oil Price Forecasts After Iran Deal
cards.teaser: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Citigroup lowered their oil price projections following the U.S.-Iran agreement on Strait of Hormuz access.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell as markets responded to a U.S.-Iran agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump announced the framework, which prompted crude oil traders to reassess supply expectations for the strategic waterway.

Major banks including Morgan Stanley adjusted their oil price forecasts downward following the diplomatic breakthrough. The agreement's potential to restore oil flows from the Persian Gulf region influenced their revised predictions.

cards.headline: Iran War Reshaped Global Economic Order
cards.teaser: The conflict between the U.S., Israel, and Iran permanently altered international economic relationships and trade patterns.
cards.body:
A deal has ended fighting between the United States, Israel, and Iran, reopening the Strait of Hormuz. However, the conflict has left thousands dead and the parties remain in largely the same positions as before the bombing campaign began.

The agreement's broader implications remain uncertain. It is unclear whether Israel will pause its offensive in Lebanon or what long-term effects the conflict will have on global trade and economic relationships.

cards.headline: Thames Water Faces Potential Nationalization
cards.teaser: The UK government objected to a proposed rescue deal for Thames Water, moving the utility company closer to public ownership.
cards.body:
Thames Water moved a step closer to nationalization after the environment secretary rejected a proposed rescue deal for the struggling utility company. The government raised concerns that the agreement did not adequately protect consumers or environmental interests.

The objection increased the likelihood that Thames Water could be taken into public ownership. The company has been seeking financial restructuring to address its difficulties, but government opposition to the current proposal leaves its future uncertain.

cards.headline: Gas Prices May Stay High Despite Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: The U.S.-Iran preliminary deal may not immediately lower fuel costs due to damaged infrastructure and transportation risks.
cards.body:
Oil prices have already dropped to three-month lows following the U.S.-Iran peace deal, with Brent crude falling about 4% to $83 per barrel. However, experts warn that prices at the pump may not decline quickly. Even if the Strait of Hormuz reopens soon, oil and gas supplies are unlikely to return to prewar levels for months.

The preliminary agreement between the U.S. and Iran addresses the greatest energy supply crisis in recent market history. Stock markets closed at record highs amid optimism about renewed Gulf oil exports. European wholesale gas prices fell 6% on the news, signaling market confidence in the breakthrough.

cards.headline: Apple releases major Siri update in iOS 27
cards.teaser: Apple launched a significant update to its voice assistant Siri with the release of iOS 27, addressing concerns about the company's position in artificial intelligence.
cards.body:
Apple introduced what it describes as a major overhaul of Siri in iOS 27, rolling out new features and capabilities for its voice assistant. The update represents the company's response to criticism about falling behind competitors in artificial intelligence development.

Analysts characterized the update as sufficient to address Apple's AI challenges, though the company now faces the test of user adoption and performance in real-world use. The release generated energy and optimism at Apple's WWDC 2026 developer conference, where executives demonstrated the new capabilities.

cards.headline: NASA prepares to launch Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
cards.teaser: NASA is preparing to launch the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, an instrument designed to survey the cosmos at speeds 1,000 times faster than the Hubble Space Telescope.
cards.body:
The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will significantly enhance NASA's space observation capabilities. The telescope can survey the cosmos roughly 1,000 times faster than the Hubble Space Telescope, enabling astronomers to map much larger portions of the universe in considerably less time.

NASA has launched a public program allowing people to submit their names for inclusion aboard the spacecraft before launch. The telescope's mirror was originally developed for spy satellite technology and is expected to transform how scientists study and understand the universe.

cards.headline: Trump administration blocks Anthropic cybersecurity AI models
cards.teaser: The Trump administration forced AI company Anthropic to pull its latest cybersecurity models from the market in a decision that signals government willingness to regulate the AI industry.

cards.headline: Study confirms continued heart protection from COVID vaccines
cards.teaser: Research shows COVID-19 vaccines continue to provide heart protection even as formulations are updated, though vaccination rates have declined amid anti-vaccine messaging.
cards.body:
A new study found that COVID-19 vaccines maintain their protective effects against heart complications despite ongoing updates to vaccine formulations. The research provides evidence supporting continued vaccination as the virus evolves.

Vaccination rates have dropped in recent periods, driven by anti-vaccine rhetoric that has spread through various media channels. The study's findings come as public health officials work to counter misinformation and encourage continued immunization against COVID-19.

cards.headline: Microsoft considers closing multiple Xbox game studios
cards.teaser: Microsoft is weighing the closure of several game development studios within its Xbox division, including Compulsion Games, Double Fine, and Ninja Theory.
cards.body:
Xbox is closing Ninja Theory, the studio behind the Hellblade series. Staff were informed of the closure on Monday, though the studio hopes to find a buyer.

The shutdown is part of a broader restructuring of Microsoft's Xbox division. Compulsion Games, developer of South of Midnight, and Double Fine are also reportedly affected by the closures.

cards.headline: Google CEO faces protests at Stanford graduation over defense contracts
cards.teaser: Sundar Pichai encountered boos and a walkout during a Stanford University graduation ceremony over Google's contracts with the Israeli government and Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
cards.body:
Students and attendees at Stanford's graduation ceremony protested Google CEO Sundar Pichai's presence, with some walking out in organized opposition. The demonstrations focused on Google's defense contracts and partnerships with the Israeli government and ICE, with particular objection to how artificial intelligence technology is deployed in these arrangements.

AI has become a focal point in college graduation protests this year as students increasingly challenge tech companies over the applications and uses of their products. The Stanford protest reflects growing activism around how major technology firms handle defense and government partnerships.

hero.headline: Tunisia fires head coach after single World Cup match
hero.body:
Tunisia dismissed head coach Sabri Lamouchi after just one game at the World Cup, appointing former Morocco and Saudi Arabia manager Herve Renard as his replacement. The decision marks one of the most abrupt coaching changes in World Cup history.

The Tunisian football federation made the announcement following the team's opening match of the tournament. Lamouchi had been in charge of the national team leading up to the World Cup, but his tenure ended after a single competitive match on the sport's biggest stage.

Renard brings significant experience to the role. He previously managed Morocco's national team and also led Saudi Arabia, giving him familiarity with African and Middle Eastern football. His appointment comes as Tunisia attempts to salvage its World Cup campaign with new leadership at the helm.

The coaching change reflects the intense pressure surrounding World Cup performance, where a single result can determine a manager's fate. National teams have limited time between group stage matches, making swift decisions necessary when federations lose confidence in their leadership. Renard will have minimal preparation time to implement his approach and tactics with the squad.

Tunisia now faces the challenge of adapting to a new coach mid-tournament. The team must quickly adjust to Renard's methods while competing against other nations in their group. The success or failure of this drastic move will be determined by Tunisia's results in their remaining group stage matches.

cards.headline: Pete Crow-Armstrong hits first cycle of 2026 MLB season
cards.teaser: Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong became the first major league player to hit for the cycle this season.
cards.body:
Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong made history by becoming the first player in Major League Baseball to hit for the cycle during the 2026 season. The cycle is one of baseball's rarest individual achievements, requiring a player to hit a single, double, triple, and home run in a single game.

Crow-Armstrong's milestone accomplishment highlights an exceptional performance that combines both hitting skill and fortunate timing during gameplay.

cards.headline: Tom Aspinall confirms September title defense against Ciryl Gane
cards.teaser: UFC heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall says he will be ready to face Frenchman Ciryl Gane in Paris in September.
cards.body:
UFC heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall has confirmed he will defend his title against Ciryl Gane in Paris this September. The British champion says he will be ready for the matchup against the French fighter.

The bout will take place on home soil for Gane, bringing the heavyweight championship to France later this year.

cards.headline: Zidane Iqbal set to become first player of Pakistani heritage at men's World Cup
cards.teaser: Former Manchester United player Zidane Iqbal will make history when he plays for Iraq this summer.
cards.body:
Zidane Iqbal, a former Manchester United player, will become the first player of Pakistani heritage to feature at a men's World Cup when he takes the field for Iraq. The midfielder's appearance at the tournament represents a significant milestone for representation in international football.

Iqbal previously played in Manchester United's youth system before transitioning to international football with Iraq. His participation at the World Cup opens new ground for players of Pakistani descent in the sport's premier tournament.

cards.headline: Brendan Sorsby to enter NFL supplemental draft
cards.teaser: Texas Tech transfer quarterback Brendan Sorsby plans to apply for the NFL's supplemental draft amid legal issues over his NCAA eligibility.
cards.body:
Texas Tech transfer quarterback Brendan Sorsby is entering the NFL's supplemental draft amid an ongoing dispute over his NCAA eligibility. The move comes after legal wrangling and challenges from the Big 12 and NCAA regarding his college eligibility status.

Sorsby's decision to pursue the supplemental draft path may effectively resolve the eligibility controversy that emerged during the offseason. The supplemental draft process accommodates players who either miss the standard draft deadline or face college eligibility complications.

cards.headline: James Dolan delivered playoff speech urging Knicks to leave nothing on the table
cards.teaser: Knicks owner James Dolan gave an impassioned speech before the playoffs, urging players to pursue a championship without reservation.
cards.body:
New York Knicks owner James Dolan addressed his team in April with an impassioned speech before the playoffs began, urging players to commit fully to pursuing a championship. He asked for a 10-week sacrifice from the roster, invoking the Spartans as he emphasized leaving nothing on the table during their postseason run.

The strategy proved effective. The Knicks won their first NBA championship in 53 years, building on the foundation of Jalen Brunson's brilliance, Mike Brown's coaching, a suffocating defense, and a healthy roster at the right time.

cards.headline: Marcelo Bielsa defends expression during World Cup photoshoot
cards.teaser: Uruguay coach Marcelo Bielsa declined to smile for the official World Cup photoshoot, saying he is not a model.
cards.body:
Marcelo Bielsa, Uruguay's head coach and former Leeds manager, defended his serious expression during the official World Cup photoshoot. When questioned about his stern appearance at the media event, Bielsa dismissed the concern by stating he is not a model.

The response underscores Bielsa's no-nonsense approach to official football duties. Known for his intense focus on tactical and competitive matters throughout his coaching career, the coach's demeanor reflects his prioritization of football over media formalities.

hero.headline: BBC Studios Partners with Japan's Kadokawa to Develop Live-Action Kiki's Delivery Service Series
hero.body:
BBC Studios Kids & Family has announced a partnership with Japanese entertainment company Kadokawa Corporation and British production company Wheel in Motion to develop a live-action television adaptation of Kiki's Delivery Service. The project marks the first time the beloved property will be adapted as a live-action television series.

The development is based on Eiko Kadono's novel, which has previously been adapted as an animated film by Studio Ghibli in 1989. The planned series will consist of 10 half-hour episodes drawn primarily from the source material. The collaboration brings together BBC Studios' international reach in children's programming with Kadokawa's deep roots in Japanese publishing and entertainment.

The original story follows a young witch named Kiki who leaves home at age 13 to spend a year living independently, as is tradition in her community. She settles in a seaside town where she starts a delivery service using her ability to fly on a broomstick. The narrative explores themes of independence, self-reliance, and finding one's place in the world.

The project represents a significant cultural crossover, combining British television production expertise with Japanese intellectual property. Kadokawa Corporation owns the rights to the original novel and has been involved in numerous adaptations of Japanese literary works. Wheel in Motion, the British production partner, brings experience in live-action family entertainment to the collaboration.

The series is currently in development, with no announced release date or casting decisions. The partnership reflects ongoing interest in adapting Japanese cultural properties for international audiences, particularly those with existing recognition from previous film adaptations. The involvement of BBC Studios suggests the series will likely target both British and international markets when completed.

cards.headline: Locarno Film Festival to Honor Asia Argento with Lifetime Achievement Award
cards.teaser: The Italian actress and director will receive the award for creative pioneers at the Swiss festival in August.
cards.body:
The Locarno Film Festival will present Italian actress and director Asia Argento with its lifetime achievement award dedicated to creative pioneers. She will receive the recognition on August 13 in the festival's outdoor Piazza Grande venue, which seats 8,000 people.

Argento will present her most recent film, Jorge Thielen Armand's Death Has No, at the ceremony. The presentation will take place at the lakeside Swiss town's main screening location, one of the festival's signature venues for major events.

cards.headline: Jon Stewart Criticizes Trump UFC White House Event While Celebrating Knicks Victory
cards.teaser: The comedian called the event a mockery while defending New York City values.
cards.body:
Jon Stewart addressed the recent UFC event held at the White House during a segment celebrating a New York Knicks win. He described the gathering as a mockery and used the moment to make broader points about American values and regional differences.

Stewart stated that there are probably more hardworking American-value individuals in the liberal hellhole of New York City than exist in the entire states of Wyoming, Idaho, and Mississippi combined. His comments tied together sports, politics, and cultural commentary in his characteristic style.

cards.headline: Tina Daheley to Depart BBC Radio 2 Breakfast Show Ahead of Sara Cox Takeover
cards.teaser: The newsreader's departure comes weeks before a planned transition in the show's hosting duties.
cards.body:
Newsreader Tina Daheley is leaving the BBC Radio 2 breakfast show, the broadcaster has announced. The move comes just a couple of weeks before Sara Cox is scheduled to take over the program in July.

The timing of Daheley's departure creates a brief transition period before Cox assumes her new role. Cox's appointment represents a shift in the breakfast show's presentation, one of Radio 2's flagship programming slots.

cards.headline: Karlovy Vary Festival Announces Central European Film Showcase and New Book Adaptation Program
cards.teaser: The festival has unveiled projects for two industry programs aimed at promoting regional cinema and literary adaptations.
cards.body:
The Karlovy Vary International Film Festival has announced the selection of works-in-progress projects from Central Europe for its KVIFF Central Stage showcase. The announcement is part of the festival's industry program, KVIFF Promises, which highlights emerging filmmaking talent from the region.

The festival also launched Book-to-Screen at KVIFF, a new initiative showcasing books seeking film adaptation deals. Eleven upcoming films were selected for the Central Stage program, which focuses on projects in development or production from Central European filmmakers.

cards.headline: The Wombles Franchise Set for Revival with New Movies and Television Series
cards.teaser: The British animated characters from the 1960s will return following consolidation of intellectual property rights.
cards.body:
The Wombles, fictional eco-conscious characters created by Elizabeth Beresford in the 1960s, are being developed for new films and television series. The Blair Partnership has been appointed as exclusive global representative following a consolidation of the brand's intellectual property rights.

The characters are furry creatures with an environmental mission who live in burrows. The revival aims to introduce The Wombles to a new generation of audiences through multiple formats including movies and television programming.

cards.headline: Aardman Director Eyes China Release for Shaun the Sheep Film
cards.teaser: Will Becher said the animated feature could reach Chinese cinemas in October while serving on a jury at Shanghai festival.
cards.body:
Aardman director Will Becher said Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom could be released in Chinese cinemas in October. He made the comments during a panel discussion at the Shanghai International Film Festival, where he is serving as chair of the animation jury.

Becher is working alongside Indian filmmaker Gitanjali Rao and Chinese animator Yu Shui on the jury. The director previously co-directed A Shaun the Sheep Movie and is currently developing a new feature film for the studio.

hero.headline: Trump and Kemp back opposing candidates in Georgia Senate primary
hero.teaser: President Trump and Georgia Governor Brian Kemp support different Republican candidates in the state's Senate primary election.
hero.body:
President Trump and Governor Brian Kemp are on opposite sides as Georgia voters go to the polls to pick a Republican nominee for Senate. Kemp backs former college football coach Derek Dooley while Trump endorses Representative Mike Collins.

The contest pits Trump against the governor of a key swing state in a test of influence within the Republican Party. The primary results will indicate which Republican leader holds more sway with Georgia voters in a race that could affect the balance of power in the Senate.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans withhold support for Trump Iran peace deal
cards.teaser: Republican senators declined to embrace President Trump's announced peace deal with Iran, telling reporters they need more information about the agreement and w.
cards.body:
Republican senators declined to embrace President Trump's announced peace deal with Iran, telling reporters they need more information about the agreement and whether it stops Iran's nuclear program before offering judgment. The hesitation marks a cautious response from Trump's own party following the United States and Israel launching strikes in February that led to a brief military conflict.

The United States and Iran are scheduled to sign a truce agreement on Friday to end hostilities in what officials have described as a brief war between the two nations. Both President Trump and Iranian leaders are known for unpredictable negotiating approaches, and the specifics of the deal have not been made public. Republican allies on Capitol Hill have maintained since the strikes began that they needed to understand the terms of any potential agreement.

The Senate Republican response reflects broader uncertainty about the consequences of the conflict and its resolution. The military engagement between the United States and Iran followed months of rising tensions in the region. Lawmakers from both parties have sought briefings on the negotiations and the framework that would govern relations between Washington and Tehran going forward.

The peace agreement comes at a sensitive political moment, with voters expressing concern about the economic fallout from the conflict. Gas prices rose during the period of military engagement, and Republicans in particular face questions about how the brief war and its aftermath will affect their standing with the electorate. Senate Republicans have indicated they will wait for the full text of the agreement and formal briefings before deciding whether to support the deal.

The White House has not released details about what concessions either side made during negotiations or what verification mechanisms the agreement includes. Republican senators told reporters they consider those details essential to evaluating whether the deal serves American national security interests and prevents Iran from developing nuclear weapons capability.

cards.headline: House Democrats plan affordability agenda if they win majority
cards.teaser: House Democrats map out a governing plan centered on lowering costs for housing, groceries, and other essentials.
cards.body:
House Democrats are mapping out a governing agenda in anticipation of potentially returning to power next year, placing affordability at the center of their pitch to voters. Economic concerns dominate the political landscape as Americans grapple with high costs for housing, groceries, and other essentials.

The military conflict with Iran and its economic effects have intensified voter focus on pocketbook issues. Democrats plan to emphasize policies aimed at reducing everyday expenses as part of their campaign strategy heading into the November elections.

cards.headline: Trump family golf course set to host Olympic event under White House arrangement
cards.teaser: Los Angeles golf course owned by Trump's family business would host the pro-am competition for the 2028 Summer Olympics.
cards.body:
Olympic organizers are working with the White House on plans for a Los Angeles golf course owned by Trump's family business to host the pro-am competition in conjunction with the 2028 Summer Olympics. The arrangement raises questions about the intersection of presidential business interests and international sporting events.

The 2028 Summer Olympics will take place in Los Angeles, and organizers are finalizing venues for various competitions and related events. The pro-am competition is a preliminary event that typically features professional golfers paired with amateurs.

cards.headline: Election officials worry Department of Homeland Security could undermine vote results
cards.teaser: Voting officials fear DHS may threaten rather than secure elections, potentially challenging results President Trump dislikes.
cards.body:
Voting officials worry the Department of Homeland Security will not serve as a partner helping to secure elections but rather as a threat seeking to undermine results that President Trump dislikes. The concerns reflect tensions between state election administrators and federal authorities over the integrity of the electoral process.

The Department of Homeland Security traditionally assists states with election security, including protection against cyber threats and foreign interference. Election officials now question whether the agency will fulfill that role or instead act to challenge outcomes unfavorable to the administration.

cards.headline: Republicans hope Iran deal lowers gas prices before elections
cards.teaser: Republicans believe the Iran peace agreement could ease fuel costs, though some fear voter perceptions of the economy are already set.
cards.body:
Gas prices spiked when the US-Iran conflict began on February 28, disrupting energy production and transportation across the Middle East. Republicans believe a peace agreement could reverse those increases and help their electoral prospects in November.

However, timing is crucial. Some Republicans close to the White House worry that voter frustration over the struggling economy may already be set, even if fuel costs decline. The vice-president indicated the agreement is preliminary—roughly a page and a half with many details to be worked out later.

cards.headline: AI deepfakes reshape campaign advertising without federal regulation
cards.teaser: Campaign ads now routinely feature AI-generated clips placing candidates in fictitious situations, with no disclosure requirements.
cards.body:
Campaign ads featuring AI-generated clips and images have become widespread, with attack ads placing candidates in compromising and fictitious situations. The largely unregulated practice warps the norms of political campaigns and blurs the line between truth and fiction.

Some campaigns voluntarily disclose AI use, but no federal requirement mandates such transparency. Democrats want to change that if they retake control of Congress in November, pushing for rules that would require campaigns to identify artificially generated content in political advertising.
